about.label: Location

about.label: Location
about.text: Sample City, Mid-Atlantic — 90 minutes by rail from two major metros; airport shuttle runs every hour on weekdays.

about.label: Setting
about.text: Suburban campus with a walkable core, wooded perimeter trails, and a downtown arts strip three blocks from the main gate.

about.label: Size
about.text: About 6,800 undergraduates and 2,100 graduate students; first-year class targets 1,650 with room for spring admits.

about.label: Ratio
about.text: Student–faculty ratio 10:1; intro lectures cap near 40, with discussion sections under 18 once majors declare.

about.label: Founded
about.text: 1887 as a polytechnic institute; university charter and research status followed in the mid-20th century.

about.label: Programs
about.text: Engineering, computer science, design, business analytics, and a selective dual-degree with the conservatory next door.

about.label: Notable
about.text: Known for co-op density, a maker-space open 24/7 during finals, and a alumni hiring pipeline into mid-Atlantic labs.

costs.label: Tuition
costs.text: Published tuition $68,400 for 2026–27 before any merit or need-based aid is applied.

costs.label: Room/board
costs.text: Standard double plus meal plan runs about $17,800; singles add roughly $2,400.

costs.label: Fees
costs.text: Student activity, health, and technology fees total about $2,100 and are rarely waived.

costs.label: Books
costs.text: Department estimate $1,250 for first-year STEM packs; many courses use inclusive-access ebooks.

costs.label: Travel
costs.text: Budget $1,400–$2,000 for two round-trips home plus local transit; city pass available at orientation.

costs.label: Net guess
costs.text: Counselor worksheet points to a mid-$40K net for a typical middle-income file if CSS is complete on time.

deadlines.label: ED
deadlines.text: Early Decision I closed Nov 1; ED II remains open through Jan 5 with midyear grades required.

deadlines.label: RD
deadlines.text: Regular Decision due Jan 15; materials must be complete by Feb 1 or the file stays incomplete.

deadlines.label: CSS
deadlines.text: CSS Profile priority Dec 1 for need-based packaging; late profiles slow March awards.

deadlines.label: FAFSA
deadlines.text: FAFSA opens in December; school code must be listed before the March packaging run.

deadlines.label: Deposit
deadlines.text: Enrollment deposit May 1; housing preference form due with the deposit or housing is lottery-only.

deadlines.label: Aid reply
deadlines.text: Aid appeal window closes April 20; new documentation must be uploaded before that date.

academics.label: USNWR
academics.text: National universities band roughly #30–#40 in the latest cycle; peer assessment is the main mover year to year.

academics.label: Program
academics.text: Undergraduate engineering sits near the top 25 nationally; CS is slightly lower but rising on placement.

academics.label: Admit rate
academics.text: Overall admit rate about 14% last cycle; ED rate roughly double RD for similar academics.

academics.label: Mid 50%
academics.text: SAT 1450–1540 / ACT 33–35 among enrolled; test-optional still available through 2027.

academics.label: GPA
academics.text: Admitted unweighted mid-50% roughly 3.85–4.0; rigor of schedule weighted heavily in review.

academics.label: Yield
academics.text: Yield near 48%; waitlist usually moves in May if deposits undershoot.

about.label: Location
about.text: Sample City, Mid-Atlantic — 90 minutes by rail from two major metros; airport shuttle runs every hour on weekdays.

about.label: Setting
about.text: Suburban campus with a walkable core, wooded perimeter trails, and a downtown arts strip three blocks from the main gate.

about.label: Size
about.text: About 6,800 undergraduates and 2,100 graduate students; first-year class targets 1,650 with room for spring admits.

about.label: Ratio
about.text: Student–faculty ratio 10:1; intro lectures cap near 40, with discussion sections under 18 once majors declare.

about.label: Founded
about.text: 1887 as a polytechnic institute; university charter and research status followed in the mid-20th century.

about.label: Programs
about.text: Engineering, computer science, design, business analytics, and a selective dual-degree with the conservatory next door.

about.label: Notable
about.text: Known for co-op density, a maker-space open 24/7 during finals, and a alumni hiring pipeline into mid-Atlantic labs.

costs.label: Tuition
costs.text: Published tuition $68,400 for 2026–27 before any merit or need-based aid is applied.

costs.label: Room/board
costs.text: Standard double plus meal plan runs about $17,800; singles add roughly $2,400.

costs.label: Fees
costs.text: Student activity, health, and technology fees total about $2,100 and are rarely waived.

costs.label: Books
costs.text: Department estimate $1,250 for first-year STEM packs; many courses use inclusive-access ebooks.

costs.label: Travel
costs.text: Budget $1,400–$2,000 for two round-trips home plus local transit; city pass available at orientation.

costs.label: Net guess
costs.text: Counselor worksheet points to a mid-$40K net for a typical middle-income file if CSS is complete on time.

deadlines.label: CSS

deadlines.label: FAFSA

deadlines.label: Deposit

deadlines.label: Aid reply

academics.label: Program

academics.label: Admit rate
academics.text: Overall admit rate about 14% last cycle; ED rate roughly double RD for similar academics.

academics.label: Mid 50%
academics.text: SAT 1450–1540 / ACT 33–35 among enrolled; test-optional still available through 2027.

academics.label: GPA

academics.label: Yield

alumni.label: Industry

alumni.label: Public

alumni.label: Arts
alumni.text: An Oscar-nominated production designer and a MacArthur fellow in materials science.

facts.label: Mascot
facts.text: The campus fox statue gets a scarf whenever the overnight temperature drops below freezing.

facts.label: Library
facts.text: Main library stays open 24 hours during finals; the quiet floor books out weeks ahead.

facts.label: Food
facts.text: Dining hall runs a late-night window until 1 a.m. on weeknights with swipe or declining balance.

facts.label: Transit
facts.text: Free campus shuttle loops every 12 minutes; light-rail stop is a seven-minute walk downhill.

internships.label: Co-op
internships.text: Optional five-year co-op: three full-time terms with average reported pay near $28/hr in engineering.

internships.label: Score
internships.text: Internship / co-op placement score 9.2/10 on the counselor sheet — among the strongest on this list.

internships.label: Extern
internships.text: January externships pair students with alumni for two-week shadowing; ~70% of first-years apply.

internships.label: Career
internships.text: Handshake posts ~1,200 exclusive roles each fall; on-campus interviews cluster in October and February.

internships.label: Outcomes
internships.text: Six-month post-grad employment or grad-school rate reported at 94% for the last audited class.

detail.counselor_take: Solid match on academics; watch net price against safer options on the list.
detail.why: Program fit and outcomes align with the plan.
detail.why_not: Cost and distance need a second look in April.

housing.label: Guarantee
housing.text: First-years are guaranteed a residence hall bed; most live on the east quad within a five-minute walk of engineering.

housing.label: Style
housing.text: Mix of traditional doubles and suite-style triples; gender-inclusive floors available by request at housing signup.

housing.label: Required
housing.text: On-campus living required for the first two years unless commuting from a permanent address within 25 miles.

housing.label: Meal plan
housing.text: All residents carry at least the 14-swipe plan; declining balance rolls term to term within the year.

why_points.label: Studio
why_points.text: Design studio access from year one with faculty who answer high-school research emails and keep shop hours open through finals week for portfolio work.

why_points.label: Co-op
why_points.text: Dense co-op hiring into labs she already shadows, with paid terms that count for credit and a counselor-tracked placement score near the top of this list.

why_points.label: Size
why_points.text: Campus still feels walkable while offering research scale, so she is not lost in a mega-lecture culture after the first year.

why_points.label: Outcomes
why_points.text: Six-month employment and grad-school rates are strong for engineering, and alumni mentors answer outreach within a week in the portal.

why_points.label: Visit
why_points.text: The overnight stay and shop tour felt honest — students talked about workload without the tour-guide gloss.

why_points.label: Culture
why_points.text: Peer energy in the makerspace is collaborative rather than cutthroat, which matches how she works on group builds today.

why_not_points.label: Intros
why_not_points.text: Large intro lectures before major declaration dilute the early studio promise and make the first two semesters feel more generic than the brochure.

why_not_points.label: Cost
why_not_points.text: Sticker without strong need-based aid is hard to justify against safer nets on this list once CSS packaging lands in March.

why_not_points.label: Climate
why_not_points.text: Winter weather is grey more than scenic for a four-year stretch, and travel home for short breaks adds friction.

why_not_points.label: Selectivity
why_not_points.text: Even with ED, the academic bar is a real reach; a deferral would force a longer LOCI cycle into a deeper RD pool.
